neighbours.label: A wh-ever word (whatever, whoever, wherever) opening a free-relative clause at the start of a sentence, vs the same sentences opened by plain what/who/where or another subordinator
fire: The lights in the barn kept flickering. Whatever caused it, the farmer wanted it fixed by Friday.
Nobody admitted to taking the last slice. Whoever ate it left the plate in the sink.
The map had been torn in half. Wherever the treasure lay, they would need the other piece.
He would not explain the bruise on his arm. Whatever had happened, he clearly did not want to talk.
The parcel came without a return address. Whoever sent it had paid for express delivery.
The dog vanished every afternoon. Wherever she went, she came back muddy and happy.
The old man muttered something in his sleep. Whatever he dreamt about, it made him smile.
The window had been forced open overnight. Whoever broke in knew exactly where the safe was.
quiet: The lights in the barn kept flickering. Because the wiring was old, the farmer wanted it fixed by Friday.
Nobody admitted to taking the last slice. The person who ate it left the plate in the sink.
The map had been torn in half. To find the treasure, they would need the other piece.
He would not explain the bruise on his arm. When asked, he clearly did not want to talk.
The parcel came without a return address. The sender had paid for express delivery.
The dog vanished every afternoon. When she returned, she came back muddy and happy.
The old man muttered something in his sleep. His dream, it seemed, made him smile.
The window had been forced open overnight. The burglar knew exactly where the safe was.

predictions: Fire items 0.4-0.9 on the wh-ever word; near misses under 0.2.
notes: Card: ' Whatever' x7, ' whatever' x4, ' whoever', 'Wherever', peaks at the comma closing the clause.
